rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-read fresh, full file, current working tree (uncommitted diff on top of HEAD fe18297). Two edits are live since the last pass: (1) a new bullet opening '## Sharpen the skill from what came back' — 'Before you ship, ask the skill itself to name its own weakest part... Push back on what it names; don't settle for reassurance.'; (2) one new maintainer-block line, 'Accept-with-mitigation (§56): no dedicated push-back move for a skipped self-critique ask. The body line above (...) is the fix; not every miss needs a trainer catch too.', placed directly after the Push-back-moves list. Neither fenced prompt was touched — the self-critique ask stays body-only, never inside author-test-strategy-skill-1 or -2. Prior pass blocked here on exactly this: a body-only ask covering the file's own named central risk (default-acceptance), with no matching push-back-move entry anywhere in this file. That gap has not moved at the mechanism level. What has moved: the maintainer has made an explicit, logged call that this is accept-with-mitigation, not an oversight — citing check_pedagogy.md §56 ('Engineer-audience audit fixes default to body callout, not forcing function... AE101... default fix-shape for audit finding = body callout') by rule number, with a stated rationale matching that rule's own logic almost verbatim. This is the same shape already load-bearing and passing elsewhere in this codebase: compound-and-close.md carries an identical pattern (a body-only push-back move, 'push back where the summary misreads', is rule 16's own named carve-out for optional push-backs, backed by an Accept-with-mitigation note citing check_pedagogy.md §50/§51) and that file's story-class instance (instances/ae101--compound-and-close.story.json) scores this PASS, not REVISE, precisely because the logged maintainer decision closes the finding. Per rule 16's own carve-out ('optional push-backs / refinements ... can live in body') and per the eval-architecture contract (rule 43d: judges are read-only; the author reconciles via /content-creation; a maintainer's Accept-with-mitigation note is the designed closing move for exactly this kind of finding), the same reasoning applies here. Cross-checked the module file one level up: earn-the-trust.md already carries a dedicated trainer catch for this exact miss — 'Ex3 default-acceptance on first SKILL.md — student ships Claude's first draft. Trainer runs the self-critique move: "ask the skill to disclose its weakest part before you ship."' — in both its Push-back-moves list AND its Per-phase-failure-mode-+-escape-hatch table, plus a Decision-points line protecting the beat from compression ('Compress Ex3's conversation phase, not the invocation-and-self-critique'). The trainer catch exists at the architecturally correct layer (module files own per-phase failure-mode tables per check_pedagogy.md rule 47; rule 64 prefers a pointer over cross-file duplication) — a duplicate entry inside this exercise file's own Push-back-moves list would restate, not add coverage. Verdict: this is a maintainer-reconciled, correctly-grounded, precedented accept, not an open mechanism gap. Flips from the prior pass's REVISE.
